findings.claim: Nested sequences still silently discard validity masks and can publish excluded pixels as VALID. Inspect sequence members recursively before NumPy coercion and add deeper-nesting regression tests.
findings.evidence: Static trace, not executed: with m=np.ma.array([100.0,300.0], mask=[False,True]), decode_linear([[m]], nodata=None) reaches the probe at line 197. The installed locked NumPy implementation (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/numpy/ma/core.py:2940–2948) reconstructs masks only from immediate children using np.asanyarray; converting the child [m] drops m's mask, so the probe sees nomask. Line 212 then produces a plain numeric array; lines 267–275 classify both positive values VALID, and line 328 publishes finite power for the masked 300 with reason NONE. The same helper serves angle and noise inputs. test_polarimetry_decode.py:574–579 tests [m], not [[m]]. This leaves the previous finding incompletely fixed and violates PRD.md:415 and :421.
